eventMetadata.context_description: Official forecasts from the UK Met Office and supporting numerical weather models indicate a maximum temperature of 23°C for London on September 5 under stable high-pressure conditions with light westerly winds, partly cloudy skies, and minimal precipitation risk. This consensus across GFS, ECMWF, and UKMO guidance, combined with observed afternoon readings near 22–23°C, underpins the market’s overwhelming 99.8% implied probability for that outcome. Historical September climatology for the region shows typical highs around 19–20°C, so the current setup reflects above-average warmth from clear skies and southerly flow. Only an abrupt increase in cloud cover or an unforecasted frontal passage could realistically cap the high below 23°C, though late-day model runs show low likelihood of such shifts before resolution.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Paris-Le Bourget Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=lfpb

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent official forecasts from the Hong Kong Observatory and supporting models point to a maximum temperature of 30–31°C on September 6, 2026, aligning with the market's leading implied probabilities of 43.5% for 31°C and 32.5% for 30°C.** 

Light winds, high humidity (70–95%), and a broad low-pressure trough are expected to bring mostly cloudy skies with scattered showers and thunderstorms, limiting solar heating and keeping the daily peak near or slightly above the early-September climatological average of ~30°C. Current observations on September 5 showed daytime readings climbing from the mid-20s°C overnight to the upper 20s–low 30s°C, consistent with the warm start to the month following August's above-normal conditions. 

The broader September outlook of normal-to-above-normal temperatures, influenced by developing El Niño conditions and warmer-than-average sea-surface temperatures in the northern South China Sea, supports the market's concentration around 30–31°C rather than higher extremes. Updated model runs and any shifts in cloud cover or convective activity ahead of resolution will be the key near-term drivers.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus from official sources and multiple models centers on a high of 34–35°C for Chengdu on September 6, 2026, aligning closely with the market’s leading outcomes (35°C at 39.5% implied probability, followed by 34°C at 21.5%).**

The Chengdu Meteorological Bureau’s September 5 outlook explicitly projects daytime highs of 34–35°C under mostly sunny to partly cloudy conditions, with light southerly winds and minimal precipitation risk. This reflects an ongoing “autumn tiger” heat episode driven by persistent high pressure, strong September insolation, and above-average temperatures (roughly 3–6°C above the month’s climatological mean of ~26–28°C). Multiple independent forecasts converge on similar values: 33–34°C (ip.cn, several apps), 34°C (local hourly models), and 35°C (some European/global runs), with limited spread indicating low near-term uncertainty.

A sharp cooldown and rain event is expected only after September 7–8 as a cold front arrives, leaving September 6 largely unaffected. Traders appear to weigh the official agency guidance and model agreement heavily, concentrating probability in the narrow 34–36°C band while assigning low odds to extremes outside recent observed trends. Resolution will hinge on the verified daily maximum from standard meteorological stations, with any last-minute model shifts or localized heating potentially nudging the exact figure within the favored range.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent southwest monsoon (habagat) activity is the dominant driver keeping Manila's September 6 daily maximum temperature centered near 29–30 °C.** Official PAGASA guidance and GFS-based forecasts show occasional to scattered rains, high cloud cover, and southwesterly flow across Metro Manila, limiting daytime heating and capping afternoon highs. Multiple model outputs and short-range guidance indicate afternoon peaks of 28–30 °C (roughly 82–86 °F) under humid, overcast conditions, consistent with the market-implied probabilities favoring 29 °C and 30 °C.  

Typical September climatology features slightly higher maxima, but the active monsoon trough and associated moisture are suppressing temperatures below seasonal norms. Traders appear to be weighting the latest official forecasts and real-time observations of widespread cloudiness and precipitation, which reduce the likelihood of clearing skies that could allow a spike toward 31 °C or higher. Updated PAGASA briefings and next model cycles will be the key near-term catalysts.

This follows several days of 90s+ readings that have given way to a cooler, more stable pattern. The implied probabilities align closely with model consensus around 76–78°F, reflecting the limited upside from the current steering pattern and absence of stronger southerly flow or clear-sky heating. Historical September 6 averages near 80°F provide context, but the fresh northeast regime has shifted trader sentiment toward the lower end of the typical range ahead of tomorrow’s final observations.

Early spring climatology supports typical September highs around 18°C, but the current cool anomaly aligns with recent observations of below-average temperatures. Updated model runs overnight will be the key near-term catalyst.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Chaudhary Charan Singh Intl Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 7 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=vilk

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Active southwest monsoon conditions, with frequent rain and thunderstorms forecast across Uttar Pradesh, represent the main driver keeping Lucknow's September 7 maximum temperature expectations clustered around 30–31 °C. Persistent cloud cover and precipitation reduce incoming solar radiation and enhance evaporative cooling, limiting daytime highs despite high humidity levels typical of the season. Official IMD outlooks and multiple numerical models project 85–90 % chances of storms on the 7th, consistent with recent days when maxima have held near 30–32 °C amid similar rainfall. Historical September averages in Lucknow hover around 32–33 °C under drier breaks, but current wetter steering patterns favor the lower end of that range. Updated model runs and IMD briefings through the weekend remain the key near-term inputs that could refine these market-implied probabilities.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Current forecasts from multiple sources, including Chinese meteorological services and international models, indicate a highest temperature in Qingdao on September 7, 2026, most likely in the 26–30°C range under stable high-pressure conditions with clear to partly cloudy skies and light northeasterly or easterly winds.** 

These patterns favor moderate daytime warming without strong advection of heat or cold air, while the coastal location and onshore flow help moderate peaks. Recent model consensus and short-range updates cluster around 28–30°C, explaining why 30°C and 31°C hold the highest implied probabilities (28% and 44.5%). 

Slight upward revisions in some ensembles support the modest edge for 31°C, though sea-breeze effects and model spread introduce realistic uncertainty that could keep the actual maximum at or below 30°C. Lower probabilities for 32°C+ or sub-29°C outcomes reflect the absence of heatwave signals or significant cooling fronts in the current pattern. New model runs and official CMA briefings over the next 48 hours will provide the key data updates for traders.
